diagnostic_evidence.quote: \mathscr{L}_n(u_n^{k+1},u_n^k,\ldots,u_n^{k+1-P}, F_n, \Delta t) = -\sum_{p=0}^{P}\alpha_p u_n^{k+1-p} + \Delta t\sum_{p=0}^{P}\beta_p F_n(u_n^{k+1-p}), \quad k = P-1, P, \ldots
\sum_{p=0}^{P}\gamma_p\uut_n^{k+p}=\Delta t N_{F_n}(\uut_n^k), \quad k=0,\ldots,P-1.

issues.failure_explanation: For P>1, a P-step method requires P starting solution values or a well-defined starter, whereas the stated DRE supplies only u_n^0. The later attempted matrix construction does not resolve this consistently: the auxiliary equations are indexed k=0,...,P-1 although Gamma is declared to have P-1 rows, and the matrices have K columns while the solution vector is declared to contain u_n^0 through u_n^K, hence K+1 entries.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply a consistent order-P starting procedure, correct all row and column counts and time indices, and include the initial-value equation in the assembled nonlinear system.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised fully approximated procedure and its matrix formulation are not well-defined for general linear multistep methods, so the corresponding general-P convergence guarantee cannot apply to the displayed algorithm as written.
issues.title: The multistep reduced problem lacks the required starting values
issues.why_classification: A standard multistep starter and consistent reindexing are local, routine repairs that can preserve the intended method and convergence order.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: It is always possible to decompose $f(p)$ into a contribution in $V$ and one in its orthogonal complement, i.e. $f(p) = f_V(p) + f_{V^\perp}(p)$.
the function $F(p): \mathbb{R}^n \to V$ defined as $F(p) = J_{\Psi'} f(p)$

issues.failure_explanation: Injectivity of J_{Psi'} on an arbitrary n-dimensional subspace V does not imply that J_{Psi'} annihilates V^perp, so J_{Psi'}f need not equal J_{Psi'}f_V. There is also a codomain mismatch: J_{Psi'}f lies in R^n, not in V subset R^N. The argument would require a complement contained in ker J_{Psi'} and a precise injectivity/homeomorphism condition on the projected parametrization.

failure_location.quote: Then $F(p) = J_{\Psi'}f_V(p)$, and invertibility of $F$ requires that $f_V(p)$ is invertible.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace V^perp by a complement adapted to ker J_{Psi'}, correct the codomain, and state the necessary injectivity and inverse-continuity conditions for the projected parametrization.
issues.overall_effect: The stated proof does not establish its characterization of manifolds admitting an injective linear encoder.
issues.title: The linear-encoder decomposition uses the wrong complementary space
issues.why_classification: The intended graph-over-a-complement characterization can be recovered by a short linear-algebraic reformulation without changing the broader method.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In fact, the decoder is only capable of reproducing linear manifolds, $\mathcal{M}\in V$
$\Psi':\mathbb{R}^N\to\mathbb{R}^n$, $m\leq n<N$

issues.failure_explanation: A linear decoder only forces the reconstructed set to lie in an n-dimensional linear subspace; it does not force the set itself to be a linear manifold. For example, with m=1 and n=2, a circle contained in a two-dimensional plane in R^N is reconstructed exactly by linear projection onto that plane and linear inclusion back into R^N.

failure_location.quote: [A linear autoencoder can reproduce with $\Varepsilon_1 = 0$ only linear manifolds]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace “only linear manifolds” by “only sets contained in an at-most n-dimensional linear subspace on which the encoder is injective.”
issues.overall_effect: The paper understates the class of manifolds that admit exact linear-autoencoder reconstruction and bases the claimed architectural classification on a false distinction.
issues.title: A linear autoencoder can exactly reconstruct nonlinear subsets of its image subspace
issues.why_classification: This is a local weakening that preserves the useful subspace limitation while correcting the false manifold classification.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the linear encoder performs a projection onto a linear subspace; the non-linear decoder can subsequently reconstruct the lost orthogonal contribution, $f_{V^\perp}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Every map admits such an orthogonal decomposition, but a decoder can reconstruct the discarded component only when the retained projection f_V uniquely identifies each manifold point. Without injectivity, two points with the same f_V and different f_{V^perp} receive the same latent code, so no decoder can reconstruct both. A circle projected to any line gives a direct example.

failure_location.quote: (A linear--non-linear autoencoder can reproduce with $\Varepsilon_1 = 0$ manifolds described by $f = f_V + f_{V^\perp}$)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the nontrivial requirement that the chosen linear projection be injective on the manifold, equivalently that the manifold be a graph over its projected image, with a continuous reconstruction map.
issues.overall_effect: The stated class of manifolds exactly representable by a linear encoder and nonlinear decoder is much too broad.
issues.title: The linear–nonlinear autoencoder proposition omits injectivity of the linear projection
issues.why_classification: Adding the missing graph/injective-projection hypothesis is a short local correction that preserves the intended construction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: there is a ReLU neural network $N_f$ with input dimension $n_{\text{in}}$, hidden layer widths at most $w$, and output dimension $n_{\text{out}}$ that $\varepsilon$-approximates $f$
We call $n$ the latent size, $\Psi':\mathbb{R}^N\to\mathbb{R}^n$, $m\leq n<N$

issues.failure_explanation: The cited theorem supplies arbitrary uniform approximation of a continuous map, not exact representation, injectivity, or an inverse decoder. Moreover, n>=m alone does not ensure that a compact m-manifold embeds in R^n; for instance, a circle cannot be continuously injected into R. Thus the proposition does not follow from the universal approximation theorem under the paper's stated latent-dimension range.

failure_location.quote: A non-linear--non-linear autoencoder can reproduce with $\Varepsilon_1 = 0$ generic manifolds\textbf{.}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require a latent dimension known to admit a topological embedding, first construct an encoder embedding and inverse on its image, and weaken finite-network exactness to approximation unless an exactly representable architecture is separately established.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed generic availability of a zero-representation-error nonlinear autoencoder is unsupported without stronger embedding and representability assumptions.
issues.title: Universal approximation does not give exact lossless encoding of generic manifolds
issues.why_classification: The result can remain recognizable, but it needs substantive embedding hypotheses and a distinction between exact topological representation and neural-network approximation.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: each layer must be injective, condition which is satisfied when $n_\ell \geq n_{\ell-1}$ for all hidden layers
By \Cref{th:uap}, we have that $n_\ell = n_\text{in}+n_\text{out}$ is sufficient to satisfy $\Varepsilon_1 = 0$

issues.failure_explanation: The dimension inequality is only a necessary rank possibility, not a sufficient condition for a layer to be injective: zero or rank-deficient weight matrices satisfy the width bound but are noninjective, and ReLU itself is noninjective. Universal approximation likewise does not ensure that an approximating network is injective or has zero representation error.

failure_location.quote: A sufficient condition for the width to ensure injectivity of the encoder is $n_\ell \geq n_\text{in}$, for $\ell = 1,\ldots, L-1$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must impose or construct full-rank affine maps and suitable injective activations, and prove that the resulting composition remains injective on the particular manifold while the final bottleneck is an embedding.
issues.overall_effect: The central architectural guideline that postponing dimensional reduction to the last layer ensures lossless encoding has no valid proof or guarantee.
issues.title: Layer width alone cannot ensure encoder injectivity
issues.why_classification: Width alone cannot be repaired into the promised injectivity guarantee by a local edit; a new injective-network construction and manifold-specific argument are required.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The parameters $\mu$ vary in a compact set with non-empty interior $\mathcal{P}\subset \mathbb{R}^{a-1}$
the map $B_r((t^*,\mu^*)) \ni (t, \mu) \to u_N$ is injective $\forall (t^*, \mu^*) \in [0,T]\times\mathcal{P}$
We conclude that $U$ is locally Euclidean

issues.failure_explanation: A compact subset of R^{a-1} with nonempty interior need not itself be a manifold or locally Euclidean at its boundary, so a neighborhood B_r intersected with [0,T]xP is not automatically an a-dimensional Euclidean chart. In addition, local injectivity of the parametrization does not exclude two distant parameter-time neighborhoods from mapping to the same state and crossing there; a locally injective figure-eight parametrization has an image that is not a manifold at the crossing. Compactness only gives a continuous inverse for an injective map on the entire compact domain, not for the claimed image structure under merely local injectivity.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require the parameter-time domain to be an a-manifold, possibly with a clearly specified boundary convention, and require a global embedding or impose compatibility conditions excluding nonlocal self-intersections.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted manifold structure and the consequent 2a+1 latent-dimension bound are not established for the parameter sets and solution maps allowed by the paper.
issues.title: Local injectivity and an arbitrary compact parameter set do not make the solution image a manifold
issues.why_classification: The repair materially narrows the advertised parameter regime and strengthens local injectivity to a global geometric condition central to the latent-dimension analysis.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Additionally, we assume that $F_N$ is bounded, with $M_{F_N} \coloneqq \sup_{u_N\in\mathcal{M}} \|F_N(u_N)\|$.

issues.failure_explanation: The estimate uses a Lipschitz constant L_{F_N}, but the proposition assumes only that F_N is bounded. Boundedness does not imply Lipschitz continuity, so the displayed estimate and the resulting uniqueness claim do not follow from the stated hypotheses.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add Lipschitz continuity of F_N on a domain containing the decoded latent states, with a uniform constant where a parameter-uniform result is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The reduced field's asserted Lipschitz continuity and the cited well-posedness theorem are unsupported under their formal assumptions.
issues.title: The reduced-vector-field Lipschitz bound assumes unstated Lipschitz continuity of the full vector field
issues.why_classification: This is a standard local hypothesis that directly validates the existing calculation without changing the method or conclusions.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $J_\Psi = (J_{\Psi'}^\top J_{\Psi'})^{-1}J_{\Psi'}^\top$
where $\Lambda$ is a square matrix whose eigenvalues have negative real part

issues.failure_explanation: First, J_{Psi'} is n-by-N with n<N, so J_{Psi'}^T J_{Psi'} is singular and the proposed inverse does not exist; the usual full-row-rank right pseudoinverse has the factors in a different order. More fundamentally, multiplying a matrix by an orthogonal projection does not generally retain a subset of its eigenvalues unless an invariant-subspace or commuting condition holds. For a general nonnormal Hurwitz matrix allowed here, a compression can even have unstable eigenvalues, so the claimed no-worse Forward Euler bound does not follow.

failure_location.quote: Due to the specific assumptions made in the construction of the decoder, the projection sets some eigenvalues to zero while leaving the others unchanged. Therefore, the eigenvalues $\neq 0$ are those of $\Lambda$, so the bound on the timestep of the \node\ is, in the worst scenario, the same as that of the \Node.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the pseudoinverse and restrict the conclusion to an appropriate setting, such as a symmetric negative-definite Lambda compressed to a subspace, or add and prove an invariant-subspace condition.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised stability preservation for an orthogonal linear autoencoder is false in the stated general Hurwitz-matrix regime.
issues.title: Orthogonal projection does not preserve the nonzero eigenvalues of a general stable matrix
issues.why_classification: A valid comparable statement survives under substantial but standard structural restrictions on Lambda or the chosen subspace; the unrestricted claim must be withdrawn.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: A necessary condition to meet the requirement $\max_{k=0,1,\ldots}\|N_{F_n}(t_k) - F_n(t_k)\| \to 0$ is that $\tau_n^k, \zeta_k \to 0$ and $\kappa \to 0$.
N_{F_n}(\mu_i, \overline{N}_{\Psi'}(\vt_{N,i}^{j+1-p}))

issues.failure_explanation: The proof identifies only necessary error limits and then declares convergence without a sufficient estimate. Even for Forward Euler, the learned field is a difference quotient of encoded data, so uniform kappa→0 is insufficient in a joint limit unless encoder errors vary as o(Delta t_train) or suitable derivative convergence is proved. For a general multistep residual, weighted combinations of field values can also have nonunique residual-zero solutions without identifiability and stability conditions. In addition, the rewrite drops kappa from the argument of N_{F_n}, changing the actual loss.

failure_location.quote: The fully data-driven is a convergent method for training $N_{F_n}$ in the sense that, under proper conditions, $\max_{k=0,1,\ldots}\|N_{F_n}(t_k) - F_n(t_k)\| \to 0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must derive a uniform sufficient error estimate for the learned field, control encoder errors relative to Delta t_train including their variation or derivatives, and establish identifiability for the chosen difference operator and sampling set.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed consistency of fully data-driven training is unproved, and the later assertion that epsilon_{F_n} tends to zero under this training strategy is unavailable.
issues.title: Zero residual and vanishing encoder error do not prove convergence of the learned vector field
issues.why_classification: The missing argument is the central convergence bridge from residual training to vector-field approximation and requires substantial new analysis rather than a local correction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: L_{\Psi}(\eps_{\Psi'}(\myw) + \eps_{F_n}(\Delta t_\text{train},\myw)T) e^{L_{F_n} T} + L_{\Psi}C_{1}\Delta t^P + \eps_{\Psi}(\myw)
So, for $|\myw|\to\infty$ and $\Delta t, \Delta t_{\text{train}} \to 0$, we have $\max_{\mu} \|\m u_N - \m \uut_N \|_{\infty} \to 0$.
Q = \|\m w_n - \m\uut_n\|_\infty \leq C_{1,\mu}\Delta t^P
By the assumption of sufficient training data and that a global minimum of the loss is reached, the term $\eps_\Psi \to 0$ as $|\myw| \to \infty$.

issues.failure_explanation: Continuity does not supply the Lipschitz constants used in the bound or uniqueness needed for the Gronwall comparison. A global minimum of an empirical loss does not imply uniform approximation over all mu, nor does increasing network size force epsilon_{Psi'}, epsilon_Psi, or epsilon_{F_n} to zero without data-density, approximation, identifiability, and optimization assumptions. The order-P estimate for discretizing the network-defined ODE also needs regularity and stability uniformly in mu and in the changing networks; its constant may depend on the network and blow up in the joint limit. Exact autoencoder reconstruction on the solution manifold is likewise not included among the theorem's hypotheses.

failure_location.quote: We make the following assumptions: $\Psi'$, $\Psi$, and $F_n$ are continuous functions; the data are generated by approximating the \Node\ using a convergent scheme, $M_N$; the training leads to the global minimum of the loss functions; we use a convergent time integration scheme $M_n$ of order $P$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must assume exact manifold encoding at the limiting level, uniform Lipschitz and smoothness bounds, a quantitatively dense training regime, uniform neural approximation and learned-field consistency estimates, and a time-discretization constant uniform in parameters and network size.
issues.overall_effect: Neither the displayed uniform error bound nor convergence in the simultaneous network-size, training-step, and online-step limits follows from the theorem's assumptions, undermining the paper's main theoretical guarantee.
issues.title: The global convergence theorem lacks the hypotheses needed for its bound and limiting claim
issues.why_classification: Establishing the advertised global, parameter-uniform convergence requires several new uniform approximation and stability arguments; merely editing a local hypothesis cannot justify the current guarantee.
